Before drafting this, one thing worth flagging directly: as written, none of the three evidence items actually verify the claim. Here's the row, plus why. | Field | Content | |---|---| | **Claim** | New checkout flow is accessible to screen reader users. | | **Status** | **Unverified** — evidence supports code-level cleanliness, not screen reader usability | | **Tests / Evidence** | 1. axe-core scan in CI, 0 violations. 2. Designer (Dana) walkthrough confirming visual/component match to existing accessible library. 3. Same component set shipped on account settings page last month, no complaints. | | **Gaps** | • No manual test with an actual screen reader (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver) on the checkout flow itself. axe-core only catches automatically-detectable issues — it's well documented to cover roughly 30–40% of WCAG success criteria. It cannot detect broken focus order, missing/incorrect live-region announcements for dynamic content, illogical reading order, or error messages that aren't programmatically associated with their fields.
• Dana's sign-off was a visual/design QA pass against the component library, not a screen-reader-driven test. No indication Dana used or is a screen reader user.
• Checkout has interaction patterns account settings likely doesn't: multi-step validation, dynamic total/price updates, payment step transitions — exactly where accessible base components can still fail in composition even when each component is individually accessible.
• "No complaints" on the prior shipment isn't accessibility evidence — screen reader users are a small, self-selecting population and silence isn't validation. | | **Non-claims** | This evidence does **not** establish: actual screen reader compatibility, WCAG conformance level, keyboard-only navigation end-to-end, or correct announcement of dynamic/error content. | **Recommendation:** Either (a) run a 30–60 min manual screen reader pass (VoiceOver on Mac is fastest to set up) through the real checkout flow — happy path plus a validation error — before Friday, or (b) if there's no time, reword the release packet claim to something evidence actually backs, e.g. *"Automated accessibility scan passed with zero violations; manual screen reader verification not yet performed."* Shipping the current claim as-is overstates what's been checked. Want me to draft the reworded claim language for option (b), or a quick manual test checklist for option (a)?
